, There are some LDP tests that have always failed.
> After fixing a few compilation errors due to method signature changes in Jersey, LDP tests fail with Jersey 2.17+.
Are you saying that there are more failures in your Jersey 2.17+ branch? Ideally, we could upgrade Jersey to resolve the memory leak issue.
If upgrading Jersey is not an option, however, we should seriously consider reverting the Jersey version.

Yes, there are a ton of 500 errors in   FedoraLdpIT, FedoraNodesIT,  FedoraTransactionsIT,  FedoraVersionsIT that appear with Jersey 2.17 (and the latest 2.22.2), but do not appear when using 2.8.  It looks like they're all related to parsing quality values.  it could very well be the case that a one-liner would fix them all, but I haven't looked that deep into it.
Caused by: java.text.ParseException: Error parsing Quality value: a decimal place is expected rather than '0'
Based on our IRC chat, if there is no loss of functionality, reverting to Jersey-2.8 seems like an easy win.

Added commit to PR which upgrades to Jersey 2.22.2.  The memory leak is fixed in this version, and I see substantial performance improvement in the GET microbenchmark.  Throughput improves by 3x, latency decreases 4-10x compared to Jersey 2.8.

Approx. 3KB of memory leaks per GET request to a Fedora container.  Heap analysis shows that this is due to an increasing number of LinkedHashMaps held by hk2, each resulting from the injection of MultiPrefer into ContentExposingResource.  This leak has likely been present since fedora 4.0.0.
It appears that this is ultimately a bug in Jersey, introduced in 2.9:
Reverting to Jersey 2.8 fixes the memory leak
It's possible that this was fixed in Jersey 2.17:

Aaron Birkland, There are some LDP tests that have always failed.
> After fixing a few compilation errors due to method signature changes in Jersey, LDP tests fail with Jersey 2.17+.
Are you saying that there are more failures in your Jersey 2.17+ branch? Ideally, we could upgrade Jersey to resolve the memory leak issue.
If upgrading Jersey is not an option, however, we should seriously consider reverting the Jersey version.

Hi Andrew,

Yes, there are a ton of 500 errors in FedoraLdpIT, FedoraNodesIT, FedoraTransactionsIT, FedoraVersionsIT that appear with Jersey 2.17 (and the latest 2.22.2), but do not appear when using 2.8. It looks like they're all related to parsing quality values. it could very well be the case that a one-liner would fix them all, but I haven't looked that deep into it.
